To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phasic contractions of juvenile pigs' urinary bladders are enhanced and are dependent on the presence of c-Kit positive interstitial cells.
The presence of PCs in juvenile mucosal strips could be due to an altered properties of IC and muscularis mucosa, and the presence of c-Kit positive ICs in the pig urinary bladder.
The presence of phasic contractions in the mucosa of juvenile pigs may reflect a greater role of interstitial cells and/or the muscularis mucosal layer in the urinary bladders of these pigs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional role of IC in the urinary bladder and the alterations that occur with maturation.
the role of ICs and their modulation in the bladder.
the functional properties of the bladder wall and its constituent layers during maturation, with the ultimate aim of improving understanding of the pathophysiology of lower urinary tract dysfunction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are differences in the functional contribution of the IC network in the juvenile and adult bladders.
the bladder of juvenile pig has a more active muscularis mucosa than the adult bladder, and the muscularis mucosal cells are the source of the phasic contractions.
there are differences in bladder properties with development, which are likely to be due to alterations in the mucosa, the muscularis mucosae and/or ICs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are significant alterations in bladder properties between juvenile and adult pigs and that ICs may play an important role in these alterations.
the bladder wall of juvenile animals has a greater ability to contract in response to cholinergic stimulation.
the muscularis mucosae and ICs are important contributors to bladder contractile function and that these components are altered with maturation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are important differences in the properties of the bladder between juvenile and adult pigs that could impact on studies of bladder function and dysfunction.
juvenile pigs may be an appropriate model to study bladder overactivity in children.
there are significant differences in the bladder of juvenile vs. adult pigs, which may be due to altered IC properties or altered properties of the muscularis mucosae.
